name: Sanctions & coercion
value: EU lists ~50 more Russian banks (16 Nov)
summary: EU listed 113 Russia-linked targets incl. nearly 50 banks on 16 Nov; a 22nd package is being prepared
state: On 16 Nov the EU listed 113 individuals and entities restricting Russia's ability to finance its war, adding nearly 50 banks and financial institutions to more than 100 already sanctioned, plus 30 individuals and two entities for information manipulation (EEAS). EU foreign policy chief Kallas said the 22nd package would be presented within days (UNN). Searches on 20 Nov found no major economy cut off from payment systems and no large seizure of sovereign assets, so Watch holds.
for_you: Firms trading with Russia or handling Russian-linked payments, shipping or insurance face tighter compliance checks. UK businesses can check current designations through OFSI guidance.
rubric_hit: Major new package: EU listed 113 targets incl. ~50 banks on 16 Nov; no payment-system cut-off of a major economy

sources.title: EEAS — The EU extends sanctions to nearly all major Russian banks
UNN — The EU will present its 22nd package of sanctions against Russia in the coming days: Kallas

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.

rubric.alert: Major economy cut off from payment systems, or large-scale seizure of sovereign assets.

rubric.normal: No major new sanctions packages this week.
